_note: Canadian credit-card surcharging rules for the surcharge decision tool. Only sourced rules ship. Anything marked 'verify-before-publishing' must be confirmed against current network documents before it is shown as fact.
framing: This tool gives general information only — not legal advice. Confirm every rule with your acquirer before surcharging.

rules.rule: Surcharging applies to credit cards only — never debit or Interac.
Surcharge capped at 2.4% or the merchant's actual cost of acceptance, whichever is lower.
rules.source: Yeeld PR, Oct 2025; Mastercard Canada merchant surcharge FAQ

rules.rule: The surcharge must be disclosed to the customer before the sale — at entry/point of sale and itemized on the receipt.
The surcharge must be refunded when the underlying purchase is refunded.

rules.note: Confirm the current registration/notice mechanics with your acquirer — processes change.
rules.rule: Merchants must register and give advance notice (30 days is the commonly cited requirement) before surcharging.

rules.note: Flagged in research; confirm with your acquirer or legal counsel before surcharging in Quebec.
rules.rule: Quebec consumer-protection nuances may further restrict surcharging.
